intro: The wider family, the new kinds of family, and the vocabulary of inheritance.
p.suegro.consejo: The feminine is «suegra». «Los suegros» are the suegro and the suegra.
p.yerno.consejo: It sounds «YER-no». Your son's wife is «la nuera».
p.nuera.consejo: It has no similar masculine: your daughter's husband is «el yerno».
p.bisabuelo.consejo: «Bis-» means «twice». Your grandchild's child is a «bisnieto».
p.pariente.consejo: False friend: «pariente» is a relative. Your parents are «los padres».
p.criar.consejo: With «se» it is growing up: «me crie con mis abuelos» (they looked after me).
p.heredar.consejo: You also inherit features: «ha heredado los ojos de su madre».
p.herencia.consejo: It comes from «heredar». The «h» is silent: «e-REN-thya».
p.testamento.consejo: You say «hacer testamento». The one who inherits is «el heredero».
p.reñir.consejo: The «e» changes to «i» in «riño», «riñes», «riñe». The «ñ» sounds «ny».
b1.titulo: Who is who in the family
b1.texto:
**By marriage.** Your partner's family is **la familia política**: **el suegro** and **la suegra**, **el cuñado** and **la cuñada**. Your daughter's husband is **el yerno**; your son's wife, **la nuera**. In formal language a husband or wife is **el cónyuge**.

**Up and down.** **El bisabuelo**, **el bisnieto**. **Los gemelos** are identical; **los mellizos** are not.

**Close and distant.** **Un pariente cercano**, **un pariente lejano**. Careful: **parientes** are relatives; your parents are **los padres**.

**Kinds of family.** **Una familia numerosa** has three or more children. **Una familia monoparental** has only one parent. **Adoptar** a child makes him or her a **hijo adoptivo**. **Criar** is looking after and educating: **me crie con mis abuelos**.

**Inheritance.** **Hacer testamento**, **heredar** a house, **repartir la herencia**. You also inherit features: **ha heredado los ojos de su madre**.

**Getting on, or not.** **Llevarse bien**, **reñir**, **hacer las paces**.
b2.f0.texto: Who is the boy in the blue shirt?
b2.f1.texto: He is my brother-in-law, my husband's brother.
b2.f2.texto: That older lady, is she your mother-in-law?
b2.f3.texto: She is a distant relative of my husband's.
b2.f4.texto: There are so many people in this house.
b2.f5.texto: We are a large family and we always eat together.
b2.f6.texto: The twins have inherited my father's eyes.
b2.f7.texto: My husband says they look like their great-grandfather.
b4.texto:
**The masculine plural** names both sexes: **los suegros** (suegro and suegra), **los hermanos**, **los tíos**, **los mellizos**.

**Reñir** changes **e** to **i**: **riño**, **riñes**, **riñe**, **reñimos**, **reñís**, **riñen**.

**Criar** takes an accent on the **í** when that vowel is stressed: **crío**, **crías**, **cría**, **crían**. In the past: **criaron**.
b4.e0.texto: My parents-in-law live in a small village.
b4.e1.texto: The siblings quarrel over the inheritance.
b4.e2.texto: My grandparents brought up five children.
b5.f0.texto: My great-grandmother's house stands at the end of the village, between a walnut tree and a stone wall.
b5.f1.texto: When she died, she left a big house and no will.
b5.f2.texto: Counting children, sons-in-law, daughters-in-law and grandchildren, the heirs were almost thirty.
b5.f3.texto: For years the siblings quarrelled over the inheritance and stopped speaking to each other.
b5.f4.texto: A sister-in-law, who is not a blood relative, suggested doing up the house together.
b5.f5.texto: Now, every August, the garden fills with voices, plates and laughter.
b5.f6.texto: More than forty relatives, close and distant, sit at one long table under the walnut tree.
b5.f7.texto: My cousin's twins run between the chairs with red cheeks.
b5.f8.texto: Both have inherited their great-grandfather's light eyes.
b5.f9.texto: So, my great-grandmother's legacy brings us together under the same roof.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the yerno is your daughter's husband.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The cuñado is your partner's brother or your sister's husband.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The suegro is your partner's father.
b7.frase: Los ____ nacen a la vez, pero no son idénticos.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: mellizos are born together but are not identical.
b7.o2.refuerzo: They are your grandchildren's children, not siblings born together.
b7.pregunta: Choose the word for non-identical siblings.
b8.frase: Es un pariente lejano de mi madre
b8.traduccion: He is a distant relative of my mother's
b9.o1.refuerzo: Your parents are «los padres», not «los parientes».
b9.o2.refuerzo: Pariente has nothing to do with business.
b10.frase: Ha ____ los ojos de su madre.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: you inherit property and also features.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Criar is looking after a child, not receiving features.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Adoptar is making a child your own; it does not work for eyes.
b10.pregunta: Which verb works for family features?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the «e» changes to «i» in the present.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is the «tú» form, not the «yo» form.
b12.pregunta: How do you say «I» with «reñir» in the present?
p.suegra.consejo: It is the feminine of «suegro». «Los suegros» are both together.
p.numerosa.consejo: It is the feminine of «numeroso». A «familia numerosa» has three or more children.
p.mellizos.consejo: Plural of «mellizo». The «ll» sounds «y» and the «z» sounds «th».
p.heredado.consejo: It is the participle of «heredar». The «h» is silent. It goes with «haber»: «ha heredado».
p.suegros.consejo: It is the masculine plural, which names the suegro and the suegra together.
p.riñen.consejo: «Reñir» changes «e» to «i». The «ñ» sounds «ny» and the initial «r» rolls strongly.
p.criaron.consejo: Past of «criar» for «ellos». It takes «-aron» like other verbs in «-ar».
p.bisabuela.consejo: It is the feminine of «bisabuelo». «Bis-» means «twice».
p.nogal.consejo: It ends in «l», so the stress falls on the last syllable with no accent.
p.muro.consejo: A «muro» is usually an outside wall or a garden wall. «Pared» is used inside a house.
p.dejó.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable. The «j» sounds like a strong h.
p.yernos.consejo: Plural of «yerno». The «y» sounds as in «yo».
p.nueras.consejo: Plural of «nuera». The «ue» is a diphthong: «NWE-ras».
p.herederos.consejo: It comes from «heredar». The «h» is silent. The woman is «heredera».
p.eran.consejo: Imperfect of «ser» for «ellos». It has no accent.
p.riñeron.consejo: In the past, «reñir» also changes «e» to «i» for «ellos»: «riñeron».
p.dejaron.consejo: «Dejar de» + infinitive is to stop doing something: «dejaron de hablarse».
p.hablarse.consejo: «Hablarse» between two people is talking to each other. The «h» is silent.
p.cuñada.consejo: It is the feminine of «cuñado». The «ñ» sounds «ny».
p.sangre.consejo: «Pariente de sangre» is someone of the same family by birth.
p.voces.consejo: Plural of «voz»: the «z» changes to «c» before «e». The «v» sounds «b».
p.lejanos.consejo: Plural of «lejano». The «j» sounds like a strong h.
p.prima.consejo: The masculine is «primo». Both together are «primos».
p.corren.consejo: The double «rr» between vowels rolls strongly. «Correr» is a regular verb.
p.claros.consejo: Plural of «claro». «Ojos claros» are light-coloured eyes.
p.nacen.consejo: For «ellos» it is «nacen»: the «c» sounds «th». Only «yo» changes: «nazco».
p.idénticos.consejo: The accent marks the «é»: «i-DÉN-ti-cos». The singular is «idéntico».
p.familiares.consejo: Here it is a noun: the people in your family. It is close to «parientes».
p.riño.consejo: It is the «yo» form of «reñir»: the «e» becomes «i».
